paper_title: DeltaEdit Enhancing Sequential Editing in Large Language Models by   Controlling Superimposed Noise
caption: : labelformat=parens, labelsep=period

model_annotations.English: This plot illustrates the relationship between an unspecified variable on the x-axis and two variables on the y-axes, specifically Efficacy top and noise E, for two different models, AlphaEdit and DeltaEdit, using the GPT2-XL model. The x-axis is labeled without a specific variable name, has a linear scale, ranges from 0 to 3000, and has tick labels at intervals of 500. The left y-axis represents Efficacy top, has a linear scale, ranges from 86 to 100, and has tick labels at intervals of 2. The right y-axis represents noise E, has a linear scale, ranges from 2 to 12, and has tick labels at intervals of 2. The plot includes four lines: AlphaEdit Efficacy top (red, dashed, square markers), which starts at approximately 99 at x=0 and decreases to around 86 at x=3000; DeltaEdit Efficacy top (blue, dashed, square markers), which begins at 99.5 at x=0 and decreases to about 94 at x=3000; AlphaEdit noise E (red, solid, square markers), which starts at around 3 at x=0 and increases to approximately 12 at x=3000; and DeltaEdit noise E (blue, solid, square markers), which begins at 3 at x=0 and rises to about 11.5 at x=3000. The AlphaEdit Efficacy top line decreases steadily, with a notable drop between x=2000 and x=3000, while the DeltaEdit Efficacy top line decreases more gradually. Both AlphaEdit noise E and DeltaEdit noise E lines increase steadily across the x-axis range.
model_annotations.German: The plot illustrates the relationship between various metrics for AlphaEdit and DeltaEdit, specifically Efficacy top and noise E, across different x-axis values, with the x-axis labeled but without units, ranging from 0 to 3000 on a linear scale with tick labels at intervals of 500. The left y-axis, labeled "Efficacy top", spans from 86 to 100 on a linear scale with tick labels at intervals of 2, while the right y-axis, labeled "noise E", ranges from 2 to 12 on a linear scale with tick labels at intervals of 2. The plot displays four lines: AlphaEdit Efficacy top (red dashed line with square markers) starts at approximately 99 at x=0, decreases gradually to around 98.5 at x=1000, and then drops more sharply to about 86 at x=3000; DeltaEdit Efficacy top (blue dashed line with square markers) begins at around 99.5 at x=0, remains relatively stable until x=1500, and then declines to approximately 94 at x=3000; AlphaEdit noise E (red solid line with square markers) starts at around 3 at x=0, increases steadily to about 12 at x=3000; DeltaEdit noise E (blue solid line with square markers) follows a similar trend to AlphaEdit noise E, starting at approximately 3 at x=0 and rising to around 11.5 at x=3000.
